gaps.quote: The restriction that matters is on movement. (cited)
gaps.note: The page never says what the movement restriction is (for example, that each step moves the head one cell). The consequence 'a value moved from one end of a tape to the other takes one step per cell crossed' is presented as following from it, but the reader cannot check it from what the page gives.

gaps.quote: Interchanging fields whose digit counts grow needs more.
gaps.note: This is a lower-bound claim that interchanging growing fields needs more than a bounded number of scans. The page only sketches a carrying strategy and never argues that no cleverer method avoids growth in passes, so the reader cannot check that the cost is forced.

gaps.quote: Counting scans therefore counts steps up to a constant factor.
gaps.note: The preceding sentence only shows a scan costs about as many steps as the cells it crosses. Counting scans gives steps up to a constant factor only if the stretches crossed are bounded in length, which the page does not say. Fields and inputs can grow, so the reader cannot check the constant-factor claim.
